mechanism_narrative: A persistently low federal funds rate (<=0.2%) compresses the risk-free rate, reducing the discount rate applied to equity valuations and generating positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days. This relationship holds in the current low-rate environment.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when FEDFUNDS <= 0.2%, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the unemployment rate above 9.5% indicates worsening labor market conditions, prompting corporate profit concerns and reducing equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when UNRATE > 9.5%, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in industrial production (INDPRO) and housing starts (HOUST) signals a broad-based economic contraction, triggering risk-off sentiment and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when both INDPRO and HOUST decline, or the interaction term's Rank IC is below 0.03 over 3-year windows.

mechanism_narrative: During periods of elevated consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL > 3.0% annualized), the Federal Reserve is likely to tighten monetary policy, increasing discount rates and reducing equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when CPIAUCSL > 3.0%, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A retail sales level above its 12-month moving average indicates robust consumer spending, boosting corporate earnings expectations and generating positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when RSAFS > 12mo_MA, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in employment (PAYEMS) and decrease in unemployment (UNRATE) indicates a strengthening labor market, which supports consumer spending and corporate profits, generating positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when PAYEMS increases and UNRATE decreases, or the interaction term's Rank IC is below 0.03 over 3-year windows.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate above 0.5% over a 3-month period indicates monetary tightening, which increases borrowing costs and reduces equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when FEDFUNDS rises > 0.5% in 3 months, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A month-over-month increase in retail sales (RSAFS) indicates immediate consumer spending strength, which is quickly reflected in equity markets, generating positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when RSAFS increases month-over-month, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.
